liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Ballad of a Thin Man** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Thin Man as their favorite Dead version of a Dylan song, calling it mesmerising; Reviewer says Thin Man was played only twice, and this version is the first set's standout [17][23]
- **Deal** (2 reviews): Reviewer considers the Deal worthy of the praise, unlike the Half Step; Attendee felt Deal was a royal flush, especially around the five-minute mark to roughly 5:35 [26][27]
- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer describes The Other One as white-knuckle hot and sizzling through to the end; Reviewer hears The Other One as a continuation of Space, with trippy, hallucinogenic vocal effects [26][27]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Reviewer calls this To Lay Me Down stellar [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-04-01.ihfm.andrewf.89939.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Static bursts occur during tuning before Half Step, and vocals are too loud at its start [1]
- **gd1988-04-01.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.90921.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 147 min [2]
- **gd1988-04-01.140934.bk411.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 22 songs; 155 min [3]
- **gd1988-04-01.sbd.miller.91160.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 149 min; rated 3.12/5 by 8 [6]
- **gd88-04-01.sbd-matrix.braverman.11264.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 143 min; rated 4.48/5 by 33 [11]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard-into-audience matrix mix well balanced and true to the band's 1988 sound; Reviewer likes the ambiance of the recording; the band sounds tight and energetic [16][17]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls friends giddy over the Minglewood, Cumberland and Deal run that closed the first set [20]
- Tickets were so scarce that someone outside offered a kitchen sink for one; reviewer, aged 15, didn't get in [22]
- Show opened with Little Bunny Foo Foo; Bobby said thanks and the band left the stage before the real start [23]
- Crowd energy comes through, with the audience going hysterical when Bobby calls them Jersey fillies [26]
- April Fool's opening featured Little Bunny Foo Foo and Itsy Bitsy Spider tuning, then Bobby saying see you later [3]
- Reviewer judges the first set among the strongest first sets of the 1980s [18]
- Reviewer finds To Lay Me Down and Thin Man more focused and tighter than at Hampton on 3/27 [18]
- Second set consists of four ordinary song pairings despite April Fools Day; reviewer prefers the first set [20]
- Setlist was not the strongest or most varied of three shows, but reviewer's favorite for its vibe [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-04-01.ihfm.andrewf.89939.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: SBD > In-house FM-mix > Sony SRF-4 FM receiver > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, w/no Dolby. Recorded inside the show, from OTS area. [1]. Also: A tape flip in Space at about 4:11 was mended together; Soundforge handled fades, levels and static smoothing; TLH was used for SBE-OK, FLAC and checksums [1]
- **gd1988-04-01.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.90921.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jon Pasternak; transferred by Andrew F; source: AUD Set One: Nakamichi CM300/CP4's > patched thru two decks > Marantz PMD-420, front row of OTS. AUD Set Two: Nakamichi CM100/CP4's > patched thru two decks >… [2]. Also: During intermission Jon moved his deck to a better taping spot; A patch from another transfer, ShnID 89939, fills the tape-flip gap in Space [2]
- **gd1988-04-01.140934.bk411.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: 1st Set: Master Audience PCM; B&K 4011 mics (1st row center, OTS)> Sony Dat > PCM (Sony PCM-F1)2nd Set: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100… [3]
- **gd1988-04-01.sbd.miller.91160.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [6]. Also: Two different soundboard cassette masters were combined to make the show complete; Joe B. Jones helped with pitch correction; Tuning, China Cat and Rider were moved to the end of the first set to fit two discs [6]
- **gd88-04-01.sbd-matrix.braverman.11264.sbeok.shnf**: source: Ultramatrix (SBD/AUD mix) [11]
